title: Sheaves and cosheaves on X as functor categories
body_html:
Sheaves and cosheaves on $X$ as functor categories

Let $\mathscr{C}$ be a category. Define

  • the category of $\mathscr{C}$-valued sheaves on $X$, $\Sh(X,\mathscr{C}) := \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X[,\mathscr{C})$;
  • the category of $\mathscr{C}$-valued cosheaves on $X$, $\Cosh(X,\mathscr{C}) := \underline{\mathrm{Fun}}([X],\mathscr{C})$.

A cosheaf is also called a (combinatorial) coefficient system in the literature.

Stalk notation. For a sheaf or cosheaf $V$ and $x \in |X|$ lying in the open cell $E$, set $V_x := V(E)$. We routinely specify $V$ via the function $x \mapsto V_x$ (constant along each open cell) together with the restriction maps $V(a)$ for face morphisms $a$.

Topological comparison. When $\mathscr{C}$ is the category of sets, abelian groups, or $R$-modules, $\underline{\mathrm{Fun}}(]X[,\mathscr{C})$ is equivalent to the category of $\mathscr{C}$-valued sheaves $V'$ on $|X|$ that are constant on each open cell. The corresponding topological sheaf is denoted $|F|$.

Lemma. With $\mathscr{C} \in \{\text{Sets, Grp, Ab, $R$-Mod}\}$ and $F$ a $\mathscr{C}$-valued sheaf on $X$, the topological sheaf $|F|$ is locally constant iff $F(a)$ is an isomorphism for every morphism $a$ in $]X[$.
